description: Edits an existing draft, scheduled or recurring notification. Pass notification_id plus ONLY the fields to change — everything else is carried over from the notification as it stands. Use this instead of pushengage_send_notification when the user wants to fix or adjust something already created ("change the title", "move it to 9am", "target a different segment"); use pushengage_send_notification to create something new. Cannot edit a notification that has already been sent or is sending, an RSS auto-push notification, or any part of an A/B test (editing one through the API breaks the test, so it is refused). Nor a notification belonging to a drip or triggered campaign, or one timezone's copy of a subscriber-timezone broadcast — manage those from the campaign or the parent. Editing a PAUSED recurring notification resumes it — the API sets the status back to running on save, exactly as the dashboard does — so tell the user that before editing one. Changing the audience replaces it entirely: pass audience_groups or subscriber_filter to set a new one. A notification with no audience goes to all subscribers — the dashboard calls that "All Subscribers" — and editing one is allowed; the response reports the audience that was saved either way, and names any audience group the API dropped because it no longer exists — the send then reaches all subscribers, so tell the user. Do not add optional fields unless the user explicitly asks to change them.

actions.description: Action buttons. Only when the user explicitly asks.

android_push.description: Android-specific options. Requires channel_id when set. Only when the user explicitly asks.

audience_groups.description: Send to one or more predefined audience groups (1-20 group IDs). Each ID refers to an audience group already configured in PushEngage. Omit this field to send to all subscribers. Only set this when the user mentions a saved/predefined audience group. Mutually exclusive with subscriber_filter.

big_image_url.description: Large hero image. Only when the user explicitly asks for a big image.

expire_in.description: Expiry in seconds (60–2419200). Only when the user explicitly asks.

image_url.description: Small notification icon. Only when the user explicitly asks for an image.

ios_push.description: iOS-specific options. Only when the user explicitly asks.

notification_id.description: The notification to edit. Get it from pushengage_list_notifications, or from the notification_id a send tool returned.

recurring_schedule.description: OPTIONAL. Turns this into a recurring notification that fires on the chosen days/times between start_date and end_date. Mutually exclusive with status="schedule", schedule_date, and send_in_subscribers_timezone. With recurring_schedule set, leave status at "sent" (default) to activate the recurrence, or use "draft" to save without activating. Only set this when the user explicitly asks for a recurring/repeating notification.

days.description: Days of the week to send on. Values are lowercase day names. At least one day required.

end_date.description: Last date the recurrence is active. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Must be on or after start_date.

start_date.description: First date the recurrence is active. Format: YYYY-MM-DD (site timezone).

times.description: Times of day to send (24-hour). HH:mm or HH:mm:ss accepted. e.g. ["09:00", "17:30"]. At least one, up to 100.

schedule_date.description: Required when status is "schedule". Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss in the site timezone.

schedule_timezone.description: OPTIONAL. The IANA timezone that `schedule_date` is written in, e.g. "Asia/Kolkata" or "America/New_York". Set this whenever the user names a timezone, or when you know their timezone differs from the site's — the notification is then scheduled for the instant they actually meant, and the response reports both wall clocks so you can tell them what was scheduled. Omit it and `schedule_date` is taken as the SITE's local time, which is what the API assumes. Requires schedule_date; cannot be combined with recurring_schedule, nor with send_in_subscribers_timezone (that flag already makes schedule_date each subscriber's own local time, so there is nothing to convert). Must be a full IANA zone name — abbreviations like "IST", "PST" or "EST" are ambiguous and are rejected, as are the Etc/GMT±N zones, whose sign is inverted.

send_in_subscribers_timezone.description: Only valid when status="schedule" (and not combined with recurring_schedule). When true, schedule_date is interpreted in each subscriber's local timezone instead of the site timezone — one delivery is scheduled per subscriber timezone so every recipient receives the push at the same wall-clock time. Only set this when the user explicitly asks for subscriber-timezone delivery (for example: "send at 9am in their timezone").

status.description: Change the delivery state. Omit to leave it as it is. Set "sent" to send a draft or a scheduled notification now, or "schedule" with a schedule_date to move it.

subscriber_filter.description: OPTIONAL. The dashboard's "Send to Custom Audience": personalize who receives this notification based on segments, location, device and more. Mutually exclusive with audience_groups; omit both for "Send to All Subscribers". A 2-D expression: `value` is a list of rule-groups, rules inside a group are AND-ed, and the top-level `op` combines the groups ("or" by default). Segment rules accept segment NAMES and are resolved automatically, so { field: "segments", op: "in", value: ["Sports Fans"] } works without a lookup. For country, state, city, device or device_type values call pushengage_list_audience_filter_values first; for an attributes rule's `key` call pushengage_list_attributes first. Both are site-specific, and a guessed value saves successfully but reaches the wrong people. Every segment reference and attribute key is verified before anything is sent; an unresolvable one fails the call rather than silently changing who receives the push. Example — mobile subscribers in the Sports Fans segment: { op: "or", value: [[{ field: "segments", op: "in", value: ["Sports Fans"] }, { field: "device", op: "in", value: ["mobile"] }]] }. Example — subscribed in the last 7 days on a paid plan: { op: "or", value: [[{ field: "ts_created", op: "ts_elapsed_lt", value: 10080 }, { field: "attributes", key: "plan", op: "ne", value: "free" }]] }.

op.description: How groups in `value` combine. Only "or" is supported: a subscriber matches if ANY group matches. Rules WITHIN a group are always AND-ed, so use one group to require several conditions together. To AND across groups, create the audience in the dashboard instead.

timezone.description: OPTIONAL. The IANA timezone that this filter's DATE values are written in, e.g. "Asia/Kolkata". Applies to absolute comparisons on ts_created / ts_last_sent / ts_last_click / ts_last_view, and to dt_gt / dt_lt on attributes. Date values in a filter are interpreted as UTC by default, so set this whenever the user gives a date in their own timezone ("subscribed after 1 January my time") — the values are converted to UTC before sending and the response reports what was converted. It does NOT affect ts_elapsed_gt / ts_elapsed_lt, which are durations in minutes and carry no timezone. Use a full zone name; abbreviations like IST or PST are rejected. Note this is unrelated to `schedule_timezone`, which concerns WHEN the notification is sent and is interpreted against the site's timezone rather than UTC.

value.description: 2-D array: outer is a list of rule-groups (max 15), each inner group is an AND-ed list of rules (1–50). With the default op="or", a subscriber matches if any group's rules all match.

field.description: Which subscriber property to match. Each field accepts only certain operators — see `op`.

key.description: Required ONLY when field="attributes" — the attribute key to look up. Call pushengage_list_attributes to discover valid keys. Must be omitted for every other field.

op.description: Comparison operator. Allowed values depend on `field`: country/state/city/device/device_type → in, nin. segments → in (any of), all (all of), nin (none of). sent_count/view_count/click_count → eq, lt, gt, lte, gte. ts_created/ts_last_sent/ts_last_view/ts_last_click → lt (before), gt (after), ts_elapsed_lt (in the last N minutes), ts_elapsed_gt (older than N minutes). profile_id/device_token_hash → in. attributes → any operator, including exists / not_exists.

value.description: The match value. Omit entirely for exists / not_exists. Array for in / nin / all. Positive integer number of MINUTES for ts_elapsed_gt / ts_elapsed_lt — 60 = one hour, 1440 = one day, 10080 = seven days. Multiply days by 1440. For segments, pass segment NAMES as strings (resolved automatically) or numeric segment IDs.

tags.description: Up to 5 tags, 36 chars each. Only when the user explicitly asks for tags.

url.description: Destination URL when the subscriber clicks the notification

utm_params.description: UTM tracking params. Only when the user explicitly asks.
